handbookNote: Georgia Real Estate Broker license exam. Exam vendor: PSI Services LLC, under contract with the Georgia Real Estate Commission (GREC) -- PRIMARY-CONFIRMED by directly fetching and reading (via pdftotext against the raw PDF, after WebFetch's own summarizer returned corrupted text) the full current GREC/PSI Candidate Information Bulletin, copyright 2026, effective 7/1/2026, from test-takers.psiexams.com/api/content/bulletin/4672. Quote: 'The Georgia Real Estate Commission has contracted with PSI Services LLC (PSI) to conduct the examination testing.' The Georgia Broker Supplement Examination's STATE portion is PRIMARY-CONFIRMED at exactly 48 items: I. State Laws and Rules (31 items: Unfair Practices, Trust Accounts, Substantive Regulations, Real Estate Practice in Georgia, Qualifications and Fees, Fair Housing Laws, Real Estate Education/Research/Recovery Fund, Complaints and Hearing Process and Attorney General's Opinions, Commission Organization and Procedures, Required Licensure); II. Management (12 items); III. Closing and Calculations (5 items). The NATIONAL portion's content-outline categories and Broker-column weights were also read directly and are PRIMARY-CONFIRMED (Property Ownership 10%, Land Use Controls 5%, Valuation 8%, Financing 9%, Contracts 19%, Agency 13%, Property Disclosures 7%, Property Management 5% with several 'BROKER ONLY' sub-items on PM trust funds/contracts/risk management, Transfer of Title 6%, Practice of Real Estate 12% with a 'BROKER ONLY' Supervisory Responsibilities sub-section, Real Estate Calculations 6%) -- notably the Broker National exam also uses scenario-based multi-option weighted-scoring items per the bulletin's own sample, a format this bank does not attempt to replicate since it doesn't map to this project's JSON schema; this bank uses conventional 4-option single-best-answer items throughout. HOWEVER, despite an exhaustive full-text read of the entire ~800-line/21-page current bulletin (every section, not just the outline), NO total question count, time-limit-in-minutes, or numeric passing-score figure is published anywhere in it for the Broker exam as a whole -- confirmed by direct search of the complete extracted text, which contains only 'up to 15 minutes' for the untimed tutorial and a '30 minutes early' arrival instruction, no exam-duration or passing-score statement. Multiple secondary sources were also fetched this session (estatepass.ai's Georgia broker page, aceableagent.com, colibrirealestate.com, theceshop.com, usrealtytraining.com, psiexams.com, pearsonvue.com) -- most 404'd or explicitly stated they did not have the figure and deferred to the GREC/PSI bulletin; the one usable figure found was estatepass.ai's own text stating Georgia broker candidates must 'Pass the PSI broker exam: 75% on each portion' (SECONDARY-CORROBORATED pass_percent=75, applied per-portion). Given this, exam_question_count=148 in the companion ga_re_broker_registry.sql is a HEDGE, not a primary figure: 48 (Georgia state portion, PRIMARY-CONFIRMED) + 100 (national portion, inferred ONLY by structural analogy to the Georgia SALESPERSON exam's national-portion count as found via a parallel research pass reading GREC's own sample Certification-of-Accuracy materials -- that 100-count is salesperson-specific and was NOT independently confirmed for the Broker national portion, which the bulletin's own content outline gives only as percentages, not a raw count). exam_duration_sec is likewise a HEDGE with NO source found this session for any total-time figure -- the companion registry SQL uses 14400 seconds (4 hours / 240 minutes) as a placeholder estimate, chosen only because a combined ~150-item national-plus-state real-estate exam commonly runs about 4 hours under PSI-administered state programs generally; this is NOT a Georgia-specific sourced figure and should be treated as an unconfirmed placeholder pending a future pass (e.g., calling GREC directly, or re-fetching once WebSearch quota resets) rather than presented to users as a confirmed exam duration. min_correct=111 is derived as the ceiling of 75% of 148, which not-coincidentally equals 75% of 100 plus 75% of 48 (75 + 36 = 111), consistent whether Georgia's actual scoring is blended or strictly per-portion. Exam fee $175 (Salesperson/Broker/CAM, identical) and license fee $170 are PRIMARY-CONFIRMED from the same bulletin. License tiers: Georgia has ONE Broker exam/license under O.C.G.A. Title 43, Chapter 40 -- JUDGMENT CALL, resolved per the build brief's specific instruction to verify this: an Associate Broker affiliates with (works under) a sponsoring Firm and receives an 'Active' license directly at the PSI test center; a Broker not immediately affiliating receives an 'Inactive' license, then separately files an 'Open A Firm' or 'Change of Qualifying Broker' application with GREC; 'Qualifying Broker' is real, GREC-recognized terminology for the broker responsible for a Firm (O.C.G.A. 43-40-9, 43-40-25). Community Association Manager (CAM) is PRIMARY-CONFIRMED as a SEPARATE, distinct GREC license (its own 48-item exam, its own 25-hour CAM Prelicense Course) that does NOT substitute for or count toward broker qualification -- a CAM must additionally complete the 75-hour Salesperson Prelicense course (or equivalent college coursework) to become a Broker. This bank targets the standard qualifying-Broker exam/license -- the single license that, depending on the licensee's choice, functions as either an Associate Broker or an independent/Qualifying Broker -- distinct from the separate CAM license, which is out of scope. Broker prerequisites, all PRIMARY-CONFIRMED directly from the current bulletin: a minimum of 3 years' active real estate licensure within the previous 5 years (quoted verbatim: 'All broker applicants must have held an active real estate license for a minimum of three years, within the previous five years, to qualify for the broker exam'); education via one of (1) a 60-hour Broker's Prelicense Course, (2) 15 quarter-hrs/9 semester-hrs of qualifying college/law-school coursework, or (3) 60 hrs of prelicense coursework approved by another state/Canadian province; a CAM applying for Broker must additionally complete the 75-hour Salesperson Prelicense course or equivalent additional college coursework; an effective 18-year-old age minimum via the required notarized Lawful Presence Affidavit; a certified Georgia Crime Information Center (GCIC) criminal history report no more than 60 days old; and a Broker/Associate-Broker-specific ENHANCED felony bar of 10 years (vs. shorter general bars) from the later of conviction, sentencing, or release from incarceration, per the GREC Background Clearance Application form. No attorney-in-lieu-of-experience/education exemption was found anywhere searched (GAC 520-1-.04, GAC 520-2, the current bulletin) -- treated as a confirmed absence, not an oversight. CE/renewal: 36 instructional hours per 4-year renewal period (effective 7/1/2015), at least 3 of those hours specifically on license-law topics (effective 7/1/2016), both PRIMARY-CONFIRMED via Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 520-1-.05 read directly. The 25-hour post-license course applies to salespersons only -- no distinct Broker post-licensing course requirement was found (confirmed absence). Per the build brief's requirement that broker content go substantially deeper than a generic salesperson bank into broker-specific territory, this 306-question bank concentrates 102 of its 306 questions (33.3%, almost exactly a third) into six broker-specific buckets: Broker Licensure Requirements & Application, Broker Office Management/Advertising/Recordkeeping, Broker Supervision & Qualifying Broker Duties, Escrow & Trust Fund Management, Commission/Compensation & Broker-Salesperson Relationships, and License Law/Commission Discipline/Recovery Fund. Real Georgia statute/rule/case citations, independently verified via direct fetch of law.justia.com's O.C.G.A. mirror, rules.sos.ga.gov's Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. Chapter 520, and law.justia.com's case reporter across this build's three parallel research passes, include: O.C.G.A. Title 43, Chapter 40 (Real Estate Brokers and Salespersons) -- 43-40-1 (broad 'Firm' definition spanning corporations/partnerships/LLCs/sole proprietorships; Property Management Services definition), 43-40-9 (firms, including nonresident corporations/LLCs, must qualify for a broker's license before affiliated licensees can be licensed under them), 43-40-11 (affiliated licensees' wall certificates held in the broker's custody/control; pocket cards), 43-40-18(a)-(d) (local-ordinance compliance for multi-location licensees; the statutory safe-harbor test shielding a broker from vicarious liability for affiliate violations when reasonable supervisory procedures existed and the broker didn't participate/ratify; the enumerated required supervisory procedures -- advertising review, license-law study programs, 30-day review of listings/contracts/leases/management agreements/offers, systematic trust-account review, compensation only to properly-firm-assigned licensees, proper trust disbursements, recordkeeping, management-availability; delegation doesn't eliminate ultimate broker responsibility), 43-40-19(a) (30-day address-change notice) and (b)-(d) (termination-of-affiliation procedure: immediate license transfer, no action pending transfer, former-broker compensation-retention rights via written agreement on enumerated pending transactions), 43-40-20(a)-(g) (trust/escrow account requirements: separate federally-insured account, one-business-day deadline for occasional trust-fund recipients, GREC bank/account notice, GREC examination rights including renewal-period exams or CPA-report substitutes, multiple accounts allowed with notice, broker NOT entitled to trust funds as commission until consummation or termination, nonresident-broker home-state-bank provision), 43-40-25(a) (GREC's sanction menu: refuse/reprimand/suspend/revoke/revoke-and-reissue-as-salesperson/cost assessments/fine up to $1,000 per violation) and 43-40-25(b) enumerated unfair trade practices (fair housing violations, misleading advertising, failure to account for/remit money, commingling, failure to maintain a trust account, non-disclosure of referral fees, unauthorized broker representation, accepting compensation outside your broker, improper dual-capacity dealing, guaranteeing resale profits, improper 'for sale' signage including a 10-day post-expiration removal rule, offering property without owner authorization, inducing breach of an existing brokerage agreement, negotiating directly with an exclusively-listed party elsewhere, calling an opinion an 'appraisal' without appraiser licensure, unlicensed practice in another state, paying commission to unlicensed persons with narrow carve-outs), 43-40-25.1 (licensees may complete listing/sales/lease contracts on attorney-prepared forms without that constituting UPL -- but this does NOT extend to deed preparation or conducting a closing), 43-40-27(a) (GREC investigations generally limited to conduct within the prior 3 years, with fraud/fiduciary-fund and pending-litigation exceptions), 43-40-30.1 (Georgia is statutorily NEUTRAL on broker-salesperson employee vs. independent-contractor status -- left entirely to the licensees' discretion), 43-40-31 (unlicensed practice or any chapter violation is a misdemeanor); Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 520-1-.06(1)(c) (net listings are CATEGORICALLY PROHIBITED in Georgia, not merely discouraged), 520-1-.07(2)-(3) (broker responsibility for affiliate violations and GREC-notification duty; a 60-day window to replace a departed qualifying broker or the firm must cease brokerage activity), 520-1-.08(1)(a)-(7) (one-month notice of additional trust accounts; 'promptly'/'as soon as practicably possible' deposit-timing language -- explicitly NOT a fixed banking-days rule, unlike some other states; interest-bearing-account written agreement; commingling permitted ONLY for bank-minimum-balance/service-charge purposes; monthly written reconciliation with 3-year record retention; enumerated proper-disbursement triggers including interpleader; refunds by check or closing credit; renewal examination via GREC form or CPA report), 520-1-.09(a)-(d) (advertising/sign rules: firm name and phone number required, must appear in equal-or-greater size/prominence/frequency than any individual licensee's); O.C.G.A. Title 10, Chapter 6A -- the Brokerage Relationships in Real Estate Transactions Act (BRRETA) -- 10-6A-1 (chapter citation), 10-6A-4(a) (BRRETA DISPLACES common-law fiduciary duty by default -- Georgia brokers owe only statutory 'reasonable care' duties unless the parties expressly agree otherwise in writing, a distinctive and heavily-tested Georgia point), 10-6A-5 through -8 (separate statutory duty sections for broker-to-seller/landlord/buyer/tenant), 10-6A-12 (dual agency expressly PERMITTED with detailed written-consent content requirements), 10-6A-13 (designated agency expressly recognized, each designated agent owing full statutory duties only to their own client); O.C.G.A. 8-3-202(a) (Georgia's fair housing protected classes: race, color, religion, sex, disability, familial status, national origin -- EXACTLY the federal FHA's 7 classes, with NO Georgia state-level additions, confirmed as an absence) and 8-3-201 (enforcement via the Georgia Commission on Equal Opportunity); O.C.G.A. 13-5-30(4) (Georgia's Statute of Frauds for land-sale contracts); 44-5-30/44-5-33 (deed execution formalities; no prescribed form required for validity), 44-5-61 (NO implied warranty of title in a Georgia land sale -- must be express) and 44-5-62 (general warranty covenant contents); 44-14-60 and 44-14-162 (Georgia uses SECURITY DEEDS, not deeds of trust -- a title-theory instrument conveying title directly to the lender/grantee with no third-party trustee -- and is a NONJUDICIAL power-of-sale foreclosure state, advertised sale 'in the usual manner of the sheriff's sales,' no court order required); 44-7-30 through 44-7-37 (Georgia landlord-tenant security deposit law: NO statutory dollar cap on deposit size, confirmed as an absence -- a genuine distinguishing fact vs. states that do cap deposits), 44-7-31 (deposit must go into a dedicated escrow account with written tenant notice), 44-7-34 (30-day return-or-itemize deadline), 44-7-35(b)-(c) (forfeiture of withholding rights for late itemization; TREBLE-damages-plus-attorney's-fees penalty for wrongful withholding, absent a bona-fide non-intentional error), 44-7-50 (dispossessory process: demand possession first, then sworn affidavit before a judge/magistrate); 48-5-7(a) (Georgia real property generally assessed at 40% of fair market value for property tax purposes), 48-5-40 (homestead exemption framework exists structurally -- no specific dollar thresholds asserted, since none were extracted this session), 48-6-1 (real estate transfer tax: $1.00 for the first $1,000 or fraction of consideration plus $0.10 per additional $100 -- customary SELLER-pays convention flagged as market practice, not statute), 48-6-61 (intangible recording tax on security deeds: $1.50 per $500 or fraction of the secured note's face amount, capped at $25,000 per note); and, for Georgia's attorney-required-closing status -- the CENTRAL, defining Georgia closing-practices fact for this bank -- In re UPL Advisory Opinion 2003-2, Supreme Court of Georgia, No. S03U1451, 588 S.E.2d 741 (Ga. 2003), decided November 10, 2003, per curiam, read directly in full: 'we have consistently held that it is the unauthorized practice of law for someone other than a duly-licensed Georgia attorney to close a real estate transaction or to prepare or facilitate the execution of such deed(s) for the benefit of a seller, borrower, or lender' -- CONFIRMING Georgia requires the physical involvement of a licensed Georgia attorney to prepare/execute the deed of conveyance and to close a real estate transaction; a title company or non-lawyer closing merely 'witnessed' by an attorney is insufficient, the attorney must actively conduct or supervise; this rests on the Supreme Court of Georgia's own exclusive constitutional authority to regulate the practice of law and its prior consistent holdings in Formal Advisory Opinion No. 86-5 (86-R9) (1989) and Formal Advisory Opinion No. 00-3 (2000). Several facts were deliberately left UNCONFIRMED/hedged rather than fabricated, consistent with this project's grounding standard: the Real Estate Education, Research and Recovery Fund's per-licensee/per-claim dollar caps (likely codified in O.C.G.A. 43-40-29/30, which could not be accessed this session -- law.justia.com and casetext.com blocked direct section-level fetches for those specific sections, and grec.state.ga.us returned HTTP 500 on every path tried); the exact statutory/rule citation barring a salesperson from serving as a firm's qualifying broker (near-universal industry knowledge, consistent with the statutory scheme confirmed, but not textually pinned down this session); GREC's trade-name registration rule (Ga. Comp. R. & Regs. 520-1-.09 by numbering convention, but its specific text could not be retrieved); Georgia's exact statutory naming of 'quitclaim deed' or 'limited/special warranty deed' as defined instrument types (the underlying mechanics are confirmed, the specific terminology is not statutorily pinned); GAR (Georgia Association of Realtors) contract-form mechanics and the widely-reported 'due diligence period' concept's exact day-counts and form number (could not be re-verified against a live source this session); whether Georgia has a specific statutory seller's-property-condition-disclosure-form mandate (not independently confirmed -- content in bucket 16 treats this as unconfirmed and relies on federal lead-based-paint disclosure law, which IS confirmed as a national/federal requirement, for its one non-hedged specific-disclosure-law fact). Standard national real-estate content not tied to a specific Georgia statute -- appraisal theory (three approaches to value, depreciation, highest-and-best-use), federal RESPA/TILA/ECOA/TRID/Fair Housing Act history and mechanics, general contract-law doctrine, real estate math formulas (commission splits, LTV, cap rate, NOI, proration, GRM, PITI, qualifying ratios), deed-type doctrine generally, general business-entity concepts, general zoning/land-use doctrine, general construction/development terminology -- is flagged 'hedge: standard...' throughout, consistent with this project's grounding standard for generic/national content. Price set at $29.99 (2999 cents) to match this project's standardized Real Estate track rate, consistent with ny_re_broker.json, pa_re_broker.json, ca_re_broker.json, fl_re_broker.json, oh_re_broker.json, and tx_re_broker.json. Answer choices were drafted correct-as-choice_a throughout across six parallel content-authoring passes (one per pair of the three broker-specific-heavy bucket groups plus three subject-matter groups, 3 buckets/51 questions per pass), then deterministically rotated into final A/B/C/D position via scripts/tracks/rotate_ga_re_broker_answers.js (global sequential-cycle rotation across all questions in file order, not manual), yielding a final distribution of A: 77 (25.2%), B: 77 (25.2%), C: 76 (24.8%), D: 76 (24.8%) across all 306 questions (18 bucket files of 17 questions each).
